newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour says still demands finmin for Cullen.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour says still demands finmin for Cullen.

text.p: New Zealand Labour leader Helen Clark said on Tuesday that her party would still insist on the finance portfolio for its finance spokesman Michael Cullen in coalition talks with the nationalist New Zealand First Party.
Clark also said she sensed signs of panic in the conservative National Party about the state of coalition negotiations.
Asked if she maintained her pre-election stance that Cullen was Labour's non-negotiable choice for finance minister, Clark said: "Nothing's changed my mind."

Clark said some members of the National Party had approached Labour in the past couple of weeks saying the two parties should discuss a National-Labour coalition, but she could not envisage this under any circumstances.

"I would...suggest to you that if the National Party was so confident about how well it was doing (in the talks), its members would not be constantly asking why we won't talk with them about a coalition," she told reporters as she entered the latest meeting with New Zealand First.
"I can think of at least half a dozen instances in the last two weeks...I sense panic, but not just in the backbench."
New Zealand First holds the balance of power after a general election on October 12 and both National and Labour are negotiating to form a coalition government with its support.
